B1:
Touched fires many times, once for each body part and contact as the character's limbs touch the part. Several events are queued before Destroy runs, and each handler adds 10 because nothing guards them. There is no debounce. Fix with a guard flag set before any yield, and do the work on the server:
```lua
local part = script.Parent
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local collected = false
part.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
  if collected then return end
  local plr = Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter(hit.Parent)
  if not plr then return end
  collected = true
  plr.leaderstats.Coins.Value += 10
  part:Destroy()
end)
```
For respawning coins, use a per-player debounce table instead and disable CanTouch while it is collected.
B2: With StreamingEnabled, the client only has instances near the player. Far-away parts of the Hotel model haven't streamed in, so dot-indexing errors. Fix 1: wait for it: `local door = workspace.Map.Buildings:WaitForChild("Hotel", 10)` then `:WaitForChild("Door", 10)` with nil checks. Better still, handle stream-out and stream-in too. Fix 2 (scalable): tag doors with CollectionService and connect through `for _, d in CS:GetTagged("Door")` plus `CS:GetInstanceAddedSignal("Door")`, with RemovedSignal for cleanup, so each door is wired up when it streams in. Alternatives: set the Hotel model's ModelStreamingMode to Atomic/Persistent (Persistent only for small essentials), or handle Touched on the server, which always has the whole map.
B3: Bugs: (1) Granted is returned even when pcall failed, so the player is charged and gets nothing. (2) There is no PurchaseId record, so Roblox retries (timeouts, shutdown, error) grant again: double coins. (3) Get-then-Set isn't atomic, so racing servers lose or duplicate updates; use UpdateAsync. (4) plr may be nil (player left), which errors on plr.UserId. Use info.PlayerId. (5) ProductId isn't checked, and the in-game coins/leaderstats aren't updated. Corrected: look up the player (if absent, return NotProcessedYet). In one UpdateAsync on the player's key, if purchases[info.PurchaseId] is already set, return unchanged; else add 100 and mark the PurchaseId. If pcall fails, return NotProcessedYet. Only on success, update the live profile and return PurchaseGranted. Unknown product: NotProcessedYet and log it.
B4: Remote arguments are serialized. Metatables aren't sent, so the client receives a plain table {Name, Ammo} without Weapon's methods, and w:Fire is nil. Functions are never sent either. Instances are sent as references, and the client can't see ServerStorage (it doesn't replicate), so Muzzle arrives as nil. Fix: send plain data (or an id) and rebuild the object on the client with a shared class module in ReplicatedStorage: `setmetatable(data, Weapon)` or `Weapon.new(data)`. Move Muzzle to ReplicatedStorage or workspace (or clone it into a replicated container first), or send an asset name/id and let the client fetch it from ReplicatedStorage.
B5:
workspace:Raycast's second argument is the ray's direction including its length. A .Unit vector is only 1 stud long, so it almost never reaches the target. The ray can also hit the shooter's own character. Fix:
```lua
local params = RaycastParams.new()
params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
params.FilterDescendantsInstances = {shooterCharacter}
local dir = (target - origin).Unit * 500 -- max range
local r = workspace:Raycast(origin, dir, params)
if r then print(r.Instance, r.Position) end
```
Or use (target - origin) directly to cast exactly to the target.
B6: When the last player leaves, the server shuts down. PlayerRemoving handlers may not finish their yielding SetAsync before the process closes, and on shutdown PlayerRemoving can be skipped entirely, so the last save is lost. Standard fix: use game:BindToClose to save every remaining player before shutdown, in parallel with task.spawn, and wait until all saves finish (about 30 s limit, aim for under 25). Make saving idempotent so PlayerRemoving and BindToClose don't double-write (track saving status per player). Use UpdateAsync with retries, plus periodic autosave so little is lost even then. In Studio, keep a short wait.

```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local UseAbility = game.ReplicatedStorage.UseAbility
local COOLDOWN = 2
local lastUse: {[Player]: number} = {}
UseAbility.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, ...)
  local now = os.clock()
  local t = lastUse[player]
  if t and now - t < COOLDOWN then return end -- spam ignored silently
  local char = player.Character
  local hum = char and char:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
  if not hum or hum.Health <= 0 then return end
  lastUse[player] = now
  -- validate any args here, then perform ability server-side

Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(p) lastUse[p] = nil end)
```

The server keeps the timestamps and the client's timing is never trusted. Clearing the entry on PlayerRemoving stops the table leaking memory.

```lua
local MPS = game:GetService("MarketplaceService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local store = game:GetService("DataStoreService"):GetDataStore("PlayerData")
local PRODUCTS = {[123456] = function(d) d.Gems = (d.Gems or 0) + 100 end} -- Gems100

  local grant = PRODUCTS[info.ProductId]
  if not grant then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
  local player = Players:GetPlayerByUserId(info.PlayerId)
  if not player then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end -- retried on rejoin
  local ok, err = pcall(function()
    store:UpdateAsync("u_" .. info.PlayerId, function(d)
      d = d or {Gems = 0, Receipts = {}}
      d.Receipts = d.Receipts or {}
      if d.Receipts[info.PurchaseId] then return d end -- already granted
      grant(d)
      d.Receipts[info.PurchaseId] = os.time()
      return d
    end)
  end)

  return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.PurchaseGranted
```

B10:
```lua
local RANGE, DAMAGE = 200, 20
local function shoot(player: Player, targetPos: Vector3)
  if typeof(targetPos) ~= "Vector3" or targetPos ~= targetPos then return end
  local char = player.Character
  local head = char and char:FindFirstChild("Head")
  local myHum = char and char:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
  if not head or not myHum or myHum.Health <= 0 then return end
  local offset = targetPos - head.Position
  if offset.Magnitude < 1e-3 then return end
  local params = RaycastParams.new()
  params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
  params.FilterDescendantsInstances = {char}
  local result = workspace:Raycast(head.Position, offset.Unit * RANGE, params)
  if not result then return end
  local model = result.Instance:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Model")
  local hum = model and model:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
  if hum and hum.Health > 0 then hum:TakeDamage(DAMAGE) end
end
```
Add a fire-rate cooldown when this is called from a remote.
B11:
```lua
local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService")
local TAG = "KillBrick"
local conns: {[Instance]: RBXScriptConnection} = {}
local function onAdded(part)
  if not part:IsA("BasePart") or conns[part] then return end
  conns[part] = part.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
    local hum = hit.Parent and hit.Parent:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
    if hum and hum.Health > 0 then hum.Health = 0 end
  end)
end
local function onRemoved(part)
  local c = conns[part]
  if c then c:Disconnect(); conns[part] = nil end
end
CollectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal(TAG):Connect(onAdded)
CollectionService:GetInstanceRemovedSignal(TAG):Connect(onRemoved)
for _, p in CollectionService:GetTagged(TAG) do onAdded(p) end
```
The removed signal also fires when a tagged part is destroyed, so the table doesn't leak.

B13: (a) Purchase: a RemoteEvent from client to server (or a RemoteFunction InvokeServer if the client needs a success/failure reply). The client sends only the itemId. The server holds the price table and the authoritative coin balance (the server-side profile), validates type, existence, balance and rate, then deducts and grants. (b) Counter: the server pushes the new balance, either by updating a replicated value (leaderstats IntValue, or an attribute on the Player the client listens to with GetAttributeChangedSignal) or with RemoteEvent:FireClient. Don't use RemoteFunction:InvokeClient: the server would yield on an untrusted client that can delay forever, error, or disconnect (an exploiter can hang the server thread), and UI updates need no reply anyway. Server-to-client should be fire-and-forget.
B14: Teleport data is sent by the client: it's visible to the client and can be modified, has size limits, and only arrives on the join (GetJoinData/GetTeleportData on the client side, or on the server via Player:GetJoinData, where TeleportData is still unverified client data). It's fine for non-sensitive hints such as the chosen loadout, map or party id, but never for balances. The coin balance belongs in the DataStore profile: save (and release the session lock) before teleporting, then load it in the match place. Use MemoryStore (a SortedMap or HashMap keyed by userId or the match/reservation id, with a short TTL) for fast, temporary, server-trusted handoff such as loadout and match assignment. Choice: DataStore for coins (persistent, authoritative). Loadout through a MemoryStore keyed by reservation, or teleport data validated on the server against owned items.
B15: Per-instance Scripts (610 copies): duplicated code that is hard to update (fixing a bug means editing 610 scripts or packages), a script VM context and memory for each, many separate connections, no central state, and they break with instances created at runtime or streamed in. Tag-driven: tag instances with CollectionService (Door, Pickup, Turret) and have one server Script or ModuleScript per tag (a component system). Each one calls GetTagged for existing instances, connects GetInstanceAddedSignal to set up an object (class instance + connections), and connects GetInstanceRemovedSignal to clean up (Disconnect, Janitor/Trove). Spawned clones that carry the tag, and client-side streaming of instances in and out, are handled automatically by the added/removed signals. Put shared config in attributes. Use a single shared Heartbeat loop for turrets, with distance gating and staggered updates. Put client-side visuals in a parallel LocalScript using the same tag pattern.
B16: Give the driver network ownership of the car (vehicle:SetNetworkOwner(driver) on the server when they sit, and back to the server or nil on exit) for smooth, responsive physics without input latency. Server ownership feels laggy. Risk: the owner's client simulates the car, so an exploiter can set any position or velocity: teleporting, speed hacks, flying, ramming others. The server must still validate: speed/position deltas against the car's max speed and acceleration (sanity checks per tick, with rubber-banding or a reset on violation), checkpoint order and lap times done server-side (Touched or region checks on the server, never client-reported), seat occupancy and who may drive, collision damage and race results. Don't trust remotes like 'I finished'. Server Authority mode (2026) is an alternative for fully server-authoritative prediction.
B17: Use an UnreliableRemoteEvent for the continuous aim/position stream. It's unordered and best effort, and it doesn't block the reliable queue. Constraints: it can drop or reorder packets; payloads over about 1,000 bytes are dropped; there is a per-client rate limit, and messages are discarded if no handler is connected. Handling: send a tick or sequence number and discard older ones. Quantize data (e.g. compact Vector3, angles to int16 in a buffer) to keep it small. Lower the rate to 10-20 Hz or send only on meaningful change, and interpolate or extrapolate on the receivers. Never send important one-time events (fire, hit, reload) unreliably; use a reliable RemoteEvent for those. The server still validates the values (clamp, sanity-check).
B18: Split the NPCs across several Actors (for example 8-16 Actors, each with a script handling a group of NPCs, or one Actor per NPC model). In each Actor, use RunService.Heartbeat:ConnectParallel (or task.desynchronize()) to do the read-only work in parallel: raycasts (workspace:Raycast is safe in parallel), path scoring and target selection. Then call task.synchronize() and apply the results (CFrame, Humanoid:MoveTo, attribute writes) in the serial phase. Limitations: most instance property writes and many APIs are not allowed in the parallel phase (they error); Actors don't share Lua state, so communicate through Actor:SendMessage/BindToMessageParallel (arguments are copied) or SharedTable (watch for races and use atomic update/increment). There's no require inside the parallel phase, scripts must be descendants of an Actor, and the overhead means tiny tasks gain nothing. Also reduce the work: run AI at about 10 Hz, stagger the NPCs, and gate by distance. Profile with the MicroProfiler first.
B19: Turn on Workspace.StreamingEnabled. Settings: StreamingMinRadius 64 (default), StreamingTargetRadius 1024 by default (lower it, e.g. 256-512, to cut memory on mobile; it must exceed the min), StreamOutBehavior = Opportunistic (frees memory), StreamingIntegrityMode = PauseOutsideLoadedArea (or MinimumRadiusPause), ModelStreamingBehavior = Improved. Per model: ModelStreamingMode Atomic for interactables that must arrive whole, Persistent only for small essentials (it adds join cost), and keep the default Nonatomic for scenery. Scripts: clients can no longer index distant parts directly. Use WaitForChild with timeouts, CollectionService GetInstanceAddedSignal/RemovedSignal to wire things up as they stream in and out, Player:RequestStreamAroundAsync before teleports or cutscenes, and keep authoritative logic on the server (which has everything). Test with a reduced target radius.
B20: Saving 80 players every 5 s means about 16 writes per second (960 per minute), above the per-server write budget (about 60 + 40 x players per minute) and the per-key write limits/cooldown, and every save happens in synchronized bursts. The 30-request queue fills, saves stall, and they then fail with errors 301-306 (for example 302: SetAsync queue full), so some saves are lost. SetAsync also overwrites blindly, risking rollbacks. Better: keep data in memory (a session-locked profile) and autosave only changed (dirty) profiles about every 60-120 s, with a random offset per player so saves are spread out. Use UpdateAsync with retry and exponential backoff and check GetRequestBudgetForRequestType. Save immediately only on important events (purchases, debounced), and on PlayerRemoving and BindToClose. A library such as ProfileStore does this for you.

Then add it to the client, e.g. `claude mcp add --scope user Roblox_Studio -- cmd.exe /c "%LOCALAPPDATA%\Roblox\mcp.bat"`, or Quick connect / JSON config, and restart the client. B22: Three core instances: InputContext (a group of actions, with Enabled, Priority and Sink), InputAction (one logical action, with Type Bool / Direction1D / 2D / 3D / ViewportPosition), and InputBinding (maps a device input such as KeyCode, gamepad button or UIButton for touch, with modifiers and Scale). An action signals through events: Pressed and Released (Bool type), StateChanged (fires on any change, for all types), or polling with action:GetState(). Precedence: give the menu's InputContext a higher Priority than the default player-scripts context and set Sink = true, so the inputs it binds are consumed and lower-priority contexts (movement or jump) don't receive them. Enable the menu context when the menu opens and disable it when it closes.
B23: It's the engine's UI styling system, which works like CSS. A StyleSheet contains StyleRules. Each StyleRule has a Selector (class names like `.Primary` via GuiObject tags, instance class like `TextButton`, `#Name`, pseudo-states like `:hover`/GuiState, `@` queries) and property values (SetProperties). StyleLink, parented under a ScreenGui (or a UI tree), points at a StyleSheet and applies its rules to that tree. StyleDerive lets one sheet inherit from another (a theme base). StyleQuery changes rules by size or input. Tokens: define them as attributes on a token or design StyleSheet (e.g. PrimaryColor = Color3) and reference them in rule properties as "$PrimaryColor". Changing the token updates every rule that uses it, which is good for theming. Don't set the same property both from scripts and from styles.
B24: The method is facial age estimation (a selfie video through Roblox's vendor, processed then deleted), with optional ID verification for 13+. It was announced Nov 2025, tested Dec 2025 in Australia, New Zealand and the Netherlands, and made global in Jan 2026; chat requires a completed age check. Age groups: under 9, 9-12, 13-15, 16-17, 18-20, 21+. Restriction: users can chat only with their own and adjacent (similar) age groups, under-9s have chat off by default, and trusted connections (verified friends) can widen this. Developers don't see ages: use TextChatService:GetChatGroupsAsync, CanUsersChatAsync and CanUsersDirectChatAsync before creating private channels, and design for players who can't chat with each other.
